speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling
text: asked the Minister for Education (a) whether the Government tracks trends in insufficient sleep among school-going children and adolescents; and (b) what measures are being considered to improve sleep health.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi) (for the Minister for Education)
text: In schools, students are taught healthy sleep habits, self-management and time management skills through Physical Education, and Character and Citizenship Education lessons.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi) (for the Minister for Education)
text: For example, students learn about the recommended sleep duration and good habits such as setting regular sleep hours, and avoiding caffeine and digital devices before bedtime.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi) (for the Minister for Education)
text: Parents too play an important part in role-modelling and developing healthy sleep habits.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi) (for the Minister for Education)
text: Through MOE's social media platforms, parents are regularly supported with tips to better manage children's screen use before bedtime.

speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
text: The first one, beyond sleep quantity, has the Ministry considered assessing sleep quality as well?

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi
text: For example, when we push back school start time, it would also mean that lessons might continue well into the afternoon when it can also be hot and humid, and perhaps less ideal for learning.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi
text: School dismissal time will also be delayed, and after-school and inter-school programmes could also be impacted.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi
text: I ask that we take a balance with regard to school start times and give the schools the specific autonomy to do so.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi
text: More importantly, we want to be able to engage our students in inculcating healthy sleep habits, including self-management and time management skills.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi
text: At the same time, it is also about working with our parents, engaging them to role model and develop healthy sleep habits at home.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi
text: And therefore, allowing our students to be able to rest well before they engage in a day of school thereafter.
